mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-16.3 to -11.6), indicating a steady recovery in shopping and recreation activity. This momentum is expected to persist mechanically over the next four weeks absent any new shock, pushing the 28-day mean higher than the prior 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -16.3 to -11.6 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean is lower than its trailing 4-week mean despite the observed three-week upward streak, the always-on momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -51.3 to -42.0 over the snapshot window. Once transit usage crosses above -40 (a threshold associated with resumed commuting and errand trips), commuters begin combining transit trips with retail stops, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -40 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -51.3 to -42.0 across four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after TRANSIT first exceeds -40, or rises before the threshold is crossed, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime where restrictions are being eased, sustained WORKPLACES recovery (from -26.3 to -16.4) signals policy-driven return-to-office mandates that structurally raise weekday foot traffic near commercial retail precincts, lifting RETAIL_REC over a full four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -26.3 to -16.4 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean fails to rise even though WORKPLACES continues improving under an active reopening regime, the policy-linked mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a compounding return of daily commuting routines; when both series improve together week-on-week, the combined effect on incidental retail visits is stronger than either series alone, producing a larger RETAIL_REC increase within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved concurrently from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward change is not larger during weeks when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve simultaneously than during weeks when only one improves, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 9.6 to 5.9, suggesting people spend less time at home. Once RESIDENTIAL falls below 6, a behavioral substitution effect occurs where freed time is redirected to out-of-home retail and recreation activity within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 6 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 9.6 to 5.9 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following RESIDENTIAL crossing below 6, the substitution threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high volatility (-9.0, 5.4, -21.0, -7.1), consistent with weather-driven outdoor activity swings typical of late-summer Sydney. Large week-on-week swings in PARKS (>15 points) signal weather disruption that temporarily displaces retail trips, reducing RETAIL_REC within one week of the swing.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change exceeds 15 points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from 5.4 to -21.0 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a PARKS swing exceeding 15 points, the seasonal volatility mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state regime with no new restriction announcements, GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable near baseline (1.7 to 3.4), indicating essential-trip behavior is unchanged. Under this stable-policy regime, RETAIL_REC growth is capped and will plateau rather than continue rising over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a narrow 1.7-3.4 range across four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean continues to rise substantially above its trailing mean despite stable GROCERY_PHARM, the plateau mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL is falling and WORKPLACES is simultaneously rising, the two trends jointly indicate a structural shift away from home-bound routines toward outside work and errands, producing a stronger and faster RETAIL_REC increase than either trend alone within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell while WORKPLACES rose concurrently from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward increase is not greater during weeks when RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises together than during weeks with only one of these trends, the interaction mechanism is rejected.
